parsed.doc_summary: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (as amended by AB 414, eff. 1/1/2026): security deposit cap of one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords), effective for deposits from 7/1/2024, plus handling, inspection, photo, itemization and return rules.

rules.title: California residential security deposit limits and handling
rules.requirement: Landlords may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent (two months if the landlord is a natural person or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total; not for service members). Landlords must photograph the unit, itemize deductions and return the deposit within 21 days after move-out, and may not call a deposit nonrefundable.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.effective_date_note: Subdivision (c)(6) applies the cap to security collected on or after July 1, 2024. The current version (AB 414) took effect 2026-01-01.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.exemptions: Two-month cap for small natural-person landlords (not applicable to service members); advance payment of 6+ months' rent allowed for leases of 6 months or longer.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security for rental agreements of residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.penalty: Bad faith retention may bring statutory damages up to twice the security amount plus actual damages; landlord forfeits claim to security if it fails in bad faith to comply with itemization/return rules.

coverage.landlord_size_condition: Two-month cap only for natural person or all-natural-person LLC landlord owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units total
unverifiable_exemptions: landlord type and number of properties owned (small landlord two-month cap)
